intent.goal: Make the per-mission behavioral eval able to fail on what the agent did to the files, not only on what its trace says: at least one fixture-backed case per mission, and a deterministic post-run check of the workspace against state the case names, without touching the routing suite or promoting eval output to proof.
intent.ruled_out: Converting existing narration-only cases in place (their prompts and assertions are routing- and narration-shaped, and rewriting them would break the brief's frozen 63 without adding a fixture); fixture files under skills/<name>/evals/fixtures/ (new paths outside the hot files; inline {path, content} entries already materialize); a model-graded state check (it would put tokens back in the pass/fail path); prose-matching on the agent's free-form narrative, except in the four cases whose prompt names a report file and a one-line verdict format; a git-backed workspace (the runner materializes files only, and making it git-init would widen scope); skipping the trace grader when state already failed (saves tokens but changes the reported shape).
intent.why: The runner already materialized fixtures into a temporary directory; the smallest change is to read that directory before it is discarded. Each check is one target and one predicate, so the case record carries the end state as data and the oracle is a few file reads with no judgement. Because every mission is a coordinator and the runner's agent has no Orca, git, or human, the picks lean on invariants the doctrine requires however far the run gets (the file the mission must never mutate, the evidence it must never forge), and not on outputs a coordinator could legitimately not produce.

noticed_not_touched: No live behavioral run was made. The suite is opt-in, spends tokens, and is not a CI gate, so the 21 new cases have been exercised by the deterministic oracle (committed tests plus the scratch untouched/good/bad pass) but not against a real headless agent. How a live agent scores on them is unmeasured.

The runner's agent (claude -p --permission-mode acceptEdits) gets a bare temporary directory: no git, no Orca, no human. Every mission is a coordinator, so the cases assert invariants and prompt-named report files, never worker output a coordinator may legitimately not produce. A richer harness (git-initialised workspace, stub Orca) would allow stronger positive checks and is out of scope.

Four positive checks read a report file whose name and one-line format the prompt gives (ATTESTATION.md, FIELD-REPORT.md, VERDICT.md; docs/DECISIONS.md is named by oss-contribute's own doctrine). These are file state, but self-reported state.
The runner writes and reads fixtures as UTF-8 text; binary fixtures are unsupported, as before this change.
